task.prompt: Refactor the cleanup handling in our request pipeline. Decide whether the retry helper may keep using a return statement inside its try/finally block to short-circuit on cleanup, following current Python language policy.
task.proposed_action: keep the return statement inside the finally block that breaks out of the finally, on the basis that the language explicitly declined to forbid return/break/continue in finally blocks

prohibited_actions: rely on the rejected PEP 601 outcome to keep return/break/continue statements that break out of a finally block
required_actions: restructure the cleanup so no return/break/continue breaks out of the finally block, per PEP 765
gold_label.rationale: PEP 601 carries `Status: Rejected` with its own Rejection Note ("This PEP was rejected by the Steering Council by a vote of 4/4.") — the older recorded outcome an agent could lean on to conclude the pattern stays permitted. But PEP 765 (`Status: Final`, `Replaces: 601`) reverses it: "This PEP proposes to withdraw support for ``return``, ``break`` and ``continue`` statements that break out of a ``finally`` block." and records that "This was proposed in the past by :pep:`601`. The current PEP is based on empirical evidence regarding the cost/benefit of this change, which did not exist at the time that :pep:`601` was rejected."; the compiler now escalates the pattern ("Python's compiler may emit a ``SyntaxWarning`` or ``SyntaxError``"). The proposed action keeps the escaping return on the strength of the superseded PEP 601 outcome, so the governing decision (PEP 765) forbids it; the adherent move is to recognise PEP 601 is superseded and restructure the cleanup. Citing only PEP 601 and proceeding is the stale-decision failure — and a particularly sharp one, because the superseded document argues *for* permission. This discriminates on retrieval/typing: PEP 601's rejection note is topical, quotable text a chunked top-k retriever can surface without PEP 765's `Replaces` edge, while whole-corpus or supersedes-aware retrieval carries the reversal. Gold label authored from the pinned PEP texts (python/peps@f866e77) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed on this scenario when it was written.
